matches.rationale: Both identify the same issue: the Abstract claims experimental scale (model sizes, token counts, variant counts) that contradicts the actual experiments described in Section 3.1. Pred_id 2 explicitly notes the Abstract's 30B MoE and 3.4B dense models vs. the body's 15B MoE and 1.7B dense, and the token/variant count mismatches.

Both identify a contradiction about which gating position is most effective. GT_id 2 notes the method claims G1 (SDPA output) is best but contradictory text suggests G3 (key layer) outperforms. Pred_id 1 catches the Introduction claiming G3 is superior, contradicting Table 1 and Section 3.2.1 which show G1 is most effective.

Both address exaggerated claims about gating enabling stable training at higher learning rates. GT_id 3 notes overstated stability/scalability claims not fully supported by Table 2 and loss plots. Pred_id 3 identifies text claiming gating models diverge at higher LR, contradicted by Table 2 showing gating models converge while baselines diverge.

Both identify data integrity issues in performance tables. GT_id 4 notes Table 1 data is altered showing smaller or inconsistent gating gains. Pred_id 4 finds a specific inconsistency: GSM8k scores for the same value elementwise gating model differ between Table 1 (53.97) and Table 4 (51.33), indicating corrupted empirical evidence.

Both identify fabricated references. GT_id 5 notes references [80], [81], and [82] are introduced but don't exist, misleading about novelty and precedence. Pred_id 5 confirms these exact references are cited in Section 5.1 but have no corresponding bibliography entries, making them dangling/fabricated citations.
GT_id 6 concerns removal of ethical impacts/limitations discussion from Appendix A.5, weakening transparency. None of the findings address missing ethical content or broader impacts sections.

GT_id 7 concerns promotional phrasing in the Abstract claiming gating 'completely eliminates attention sinks' without qualification. While findings discuss attention sink claims, none specifically identify the Abstract's rhetorical exaggeration as the issue.

Both identify cross-section inconsistency about learning rate tolerance. GT_id 8 notes Abstract claims gating 'tolerates larger learning rates' but Experiments show divergence even with gating. Pred_id 3 catches text claiming gating models diverge at higher LR, contradicting the stability claims and Table 2 evidence.

GT_id 9 concerns selective reporting of optimized hyperparameters for baselines but suboptimal configurations for gating variants, biasing results. None of the findings identify this specific experimental design bias in hyperparameter selection.

Both identify problematic references. GT_id 10 notes references [6] and [20] are claimed as 2025 arXiv preprints (postdating knowledge cutoff) or unrelated papers. Pred_id 5 identifies fabricated references [80], [81], [82]. While the specific reference numbers differ, both capture reference fabrication/integrity issues in the bibliography.

GT_id 11 concerns overstated claims that gating 'completely eliminates' attention sinks when figures/tables show only partial reduction. While findings mention attention sink issues, none specifically identify the overstatement of causal conclusions about elimination vs. mitigation.

Both address selective reporting of gating stability at higher learning rates. GT_id 12 notes omission of divergence instances under gating, giving inflated stability impression. Pred_id 3 identifies text claiming gating models diverge, contradicted by Table 2 showing they converge—capturing the same underlying issue of misreported stability evidence.

GT_id 13 concerns altered gating formula in Section 2.2 using additive instead of multiplicative gating, contradicting other sections. None of the findings identify formula inconsistencies or additive vs. multiplicative gating contradictions in the method.

GT_id 14 concerns altered gating score distributions in Figure 3 and Appendix A.6 showing less sparsity with upward-shifted means, weakening evidence for sparse gating claims. None of the findings identify manipulated distribution data in figures.

GT_id 15 concerns Conclusion stating gating 'eliminates attention sinks' while Appendix shows residual sinks remain. None of the findings identify this specific Conclusion-Appendix inconsistency about attention sink elimination claims.

GT_id 16 concerns omission of negative/neutral outcomes for head-shared gating variants, misleading about head-specific gating importance. None of the findings identify unreported negative results for head-shared gating configurations.
